title: Discovery of 2D Superatomic Mixed Crystal via Encapsulated Growth Inside a Scanning Transmission Electron Microscope
content: Superatoms are atomically precise clusters that exhibit electronic and chemical properties analogous to those of individual atoms, effectively serving as elemental units beyond the conventional periodic table. The concept of superatoms emerged from early studies on metal clusters, particularly the discovery that certain stable clusters, such as aluminum anions, display discrete electronic shells reminiscent of noble gases [1]. This behavior can be understood within the framework of the jellium model, where delocalized electrons occupy quantized energy levels similar to atomic orbitals [2-3]. Over the past few decades, superatomic materials have gained interest for their tunable electronic properties, functional catalysts, and potential in next-generation devices [4]. Recent studies on the Au₆Te₁2Se₈ superatomic system have revealed the emergence of a superatomic charge-density wave (S-CDW) phase, demonstrating that collective electron behavior extends to these hierarchical materials [5]. Unlike conventional atomic-scale CDW transitions, this superatomic CDW phase forms at ultra-low pressure (0.1 GPa), nearly two orders of magnitude lower than typical atomic systems. Notably, this Au₆Te₁2Se₈ system geometry closely resembles the geometry of the 3D Pd3Se10 system [6].
